rules.condition: a request has a wrong opcode
rules.statement: TL-UL devices must raise a runtime error via d_error when a request carries a wrong opcode.
a_size must not be greater than 2; a request violating this is flagged by the device with d_error.
Inactive lanes must be marked with 'b0 in a_mask; otherwise the request has a wrong a_addr/a_size/a_mask combination and raises d_error.
PutFullData must mark all active lanes with a 'b1 in a_mask.
A non-contiguous a_mask may lead to an error response, depending on device support.
Register files always assume aligned 32-bit accesses; other accesses are in violation.

rules.condition: a request accesses a non-existent address
rules.statement: TL-UL devices must raise d_error for accesses to non-existent addresses.

rules.condition: a response is orphaned (no valid request counterpart) or has the wrong opcode
rules.statement: The host side must discard orphaned responses and responses with the wrong opcode.
Raising a critical hardware error on these violations is planned but not yet implemented.
Devices and hosts may implement additional more restrictive checks if needed.
